Well, there's quite a number of ways one could integrate the two. I've
developed a pure web services way with REDCap, a data collection tool
for researchers:

http://project-redcap.org/

It's written in php and makes web service style calls to rapache,
delivering both graphics and textual summary statistics. Here's a
crude diagram:

php <----> rapache
 ^
 |
 |
v
browser

I'll see if I can get permission to post the documentation somewhere
public.

Another way is to use a hybrid approach whereby the web app integrates
the two within the delivered html. I used this approach for the RoR/
rapache polyart app here:

http://polyart.rapache.net/

source here:

http://polyart.rapache.net/polyart_dist.tgz

and the crude diagram is:

RoR <---> rapache
^              A
|             /
|           /
|         /
|       /
v    A
browser

I'm working off the top of my head here since it's been so long since
I wrote that app, but essentially RoR builds a web page which has html
form elements that posts to rapache, I think there's also javascript
calls as well. Also I believe there are some form posts to RoR which
then call rapache.

Jeff

messages.subject: Re: best way to load packages
messages.body_plain:
Hi Roger,

What you want to do is use the lib argument to install.packages() or
the -l (long form is --library=) argument to R CMD INSTALL. I'll
explain further:

>From within R, you can call install.packages('brew') and that will
install brew in the first path that's located in the variable
.libPaths(). For instance on my machine, it's:

> .libPaths()
[1] "/home/hornerj/Rlib/2.10.1"     "/usr/local/lib/R/site-library"
[3] "/usr/lib/R/site-library"       "/usr/lib/R/library"

So, in this case brew will be installed in my home area just like on
your machine. Changing the command to
install.packages('brew',lib='/usr/lib/R/site-library') will install
brew into R's site library.

>From the command line, and if you downloaded brew as source, then the
same thing will happen with R CMD INSTALL brew; R is going to pick the
first library path in .libPaths(), so you will want to call R CMD
INSTALL -l /usr/lib/R/site-library brew.

In both of the options above, you will want to make sure and run those
commands as root since directories like /usr/lib/R/site-library are
always protected.

Best,

Jeff

messages.subject: Rapache seg-fault resolution: beware if using myodbc + RODBC + Rapache.
messages.subject_clean: Rapache seg-fault resolution: beware if using myodbc + RODBC + Rapache.
messages.body_plain:
Hi there Jeff et al.,

Don't know if this is worth posting.  You decide.

You may recall that I posted a note seeking help in understanding why
Rapache was causing a seg-fault in the thread of Apache where it was
running. Since this was an isolated incident, it was unlikely that it
had anything to do with Rapache.  In fact, it was caused by the
unixODBC driver manager, which did not provide Unicode support for the
mysql odbc driver (it's far better to use the RMySQL package and avoid
the complications, but we want to be dbms-agnostic).  The bug is known
to the developers of the mysql odbc driver, who recommend as a
solution to use the version 3.51 of the mysql odbc driver (requires no
Unicode support) or version 2.2.12 or newer of the unixODBC driver
manager (or some other manager that provides the support).  In our
install, Rapache worked fine until it ran an R script that queried
data.

Cheers,

Leo

messages.body_plain:
Hi Rajarshi,

Sorry it took so long to respond...

Looks like there may be issues with your setup. Maybe your OS needs an
update, maybe just the libc libraries. I don't know. I tested the
following rapache handler on Ubuntu jaunty (9.04) 64bit, R 2.10.0,
rapache 1.1.8, and RSQLite 0.8-4 and it works like a champ:

library(RSQLite)
library(datasets)
handler <- function(){
    setContentType('text/plain')
    conn <- dbConnect(SQLite(),dbname='/tmp/
sqlite_test',flags=SQLITE_RWC)
    dbWriteTable(conn,'iris',iris)
    print(dbReadTable(conn,'iris'))
    dbDisconnect(conn)
}

Best,

Jeff

messages.subject: [announce] yeroon.net/ggplot2 web application v0.2
messages.body_plain:
A new version of the ggplot2 web interface has been released. Info and
a demo video are available here: http://www.stat.ucla.edu/~jeroen/ggplot2/.
The new version has a lot of cool new features, like advanced data
import, integration with Google docs, converting variables from
numeric to factor to dates and vice versa, and a lot of new geom's.

For those that missed it: yeroon.net/ggplot2 <http://yeroon.net/ggplot2> is a web interface for
Hadley Wickham's R package ggplot2. It is used as a tool for rapid
prototyping, exploratory graphical analysis and education of
statistics and R. The interface is written completely in javascript,
therefore there is no need to install anything on the client side: a
standard browser will do. All major browsers are supported but a
recent and standards-compliant browser is highly recommended. Best
performance is achieved by using Google Chrome.

The easiest way to learn how to use the application is by taking 5
minutes to watch the introductory demo video.

messages.body_plain:
The problem is a problem in IE, not Apache. My advice: don't use the .rhtml extension. You don't need it and it confuses IE in a way that it will think it has to download the file instead of display it. Best way to name your rapache scripts is either matching the extention with the content type (e.g. 'html', or 'png' if an image is returned) or what I usually do not giving them an extension at all. Works for all browsers.
